name: station-default
description: Veritas 1.5 Repo Standards for Station. Originally migrated from the 0.3 policy pack; product-specific structural checks remain npm proof lanes until they prove reusable. See docs/strategy/veritas/migration-0.5-record.md for the historical dispositions. The four delivery-conduct rules added 2026-08-01 (trust surfaces, evidence routing, read-path joins, verification conduct) codify docs/strategy/multi-agent-delivery-protocol.md as just-in-time agent guidance; their deterministic part is the existence of the surface and of the pinned regression tests that already prove each rule in `npm run ci:fast`. EVERY rule now carries the 1.5 `enforcementLevel` field and none carries `stage` (station#1480, station#1561, kontourai/veritas#188): `stage` was never in the 1.5 schema, the runtime ignores undefined fields, and src/rules/result.mjs passes `enforcementLevel` straight through — so a rule without it can never be blocking. The four pre-1.5 rules had therefore been advisory since the 1.5 migration despite reading `"stage": "block"`. Their migration is a per-rule human enforcement decision, not a mechanical translation: block -> Require for `required-station-governance-artifacts` (19/19 artifacts present) and `forbid-shared-root-imports` (0 matches across every governed source root), warn/recommend -> Guide for `ai-instruction-files-synced` and `brownfield-gap-log-present`, which 1.5 cannot distinguish because both are non-blocking. `trust-surfaces-name-their-gaps` and `verification-conduct-sentinels-and-fault-injection` are promoted Guide -> Require on the station#1480 owner-approved plan; the latter's `match.artifacts` was narrowed from seven entries to five first, because arming a list that cannot fail is ceremony (reasoning per entry is in that rule's explain.summary). `evidence-claims-anchor-to-executed-commands` and `read-paths-join-exactly-and-never-write` stay at Guide, and their original ~2026-08-15 date gate is replaced by an evidence trigger recorded in each rule's explain.summary: assess for Require on the first in-scope catch in docs/strategy/catches/catches.jsonl dated on or after 2026-08-01. Promotion buys exactly one thing for a required-artifacts rule and the claim is deliberately narrow: deleting a named surface or a pinned honesty test becomes a readiness FAIL instead of a warning. It does NOT make the rule detect the conduct it describes, and it does not change guidance delivery — src/explain.mjs serves the rule block at every level. Further promotions follow docs/strategy/veritas/proof-family-promotion-workflow.md.

rules.message: Required Station governance, CI, and Veritas artifacts must exist.

explain.summary: Keep the repository trust contract present: Veritas 1.5 governance baseline, CI workflows, issue/PR templates, security and contract docs.
mustDo: Restore any missing governance, CI, or Veritas artifact before finishing.
mustNotDo: Do not delete or weaken governance files to make a readiness run pass.
explain.exampleGood: Update .veritas/repo-map.json and this standards file together when the repo layout changes.

rules.message: Agent instruction files must include the Veritas governance block.

explain.summary: AGENTS.md (and its CLAUDE.md symlink) must carry the canonical marker-bounded governance block.
mustDo: Reapply the governance block (veritas apply governance-blocks) after editing instruction files.
mustNotDo: Do not hand-edit the marker-bounded block into a different meaning.
explain.exampleGood: Keep Station-specific notes outside the marker block and regenerate the block.
explain.exampleBad: Delete the governance block from AGENTS.md.

rules.message: New code must not import from the @kontourai/station-shared root; use @kontourai/station-contracts/* or explicit helper subpaths.

explain.summary: Contract types are owned by @kontourai/station-contracts; shared helpers are imported via explicit subpaths (e.g. @kontourai/station-shared/build).
mustDo: Import contract types from @kontourai/station-contracts/* and helpers from @kontourai/station-shared/<subpath>.
mustNotDo: Do not import from the bare @kontourai/station-shared package root (nor the legacy @stallion-ai/shared root).

rules.message: Brownfield Veritas adoption should keep the gap log and migration record so local workarounds can become Veritas product improvements.

explain.summary: Record Veritas product gaps and migration dispositions instead of hiding them in one-off workarounds.
mustDo: Append to the gap log when Veritas lacks a needed abstraction.
mustNotDo: Do not silently drop a previously required protection without a recorded disposition.
explain.exampleBad: Delete the migration record after the migration lands.

rules.message: Trust and provenance surfaces render a missing fact as an explicit named gap, and derive per-record claims from that record's own data.

explain.summary: Any surface that makes a claim about a turn, run, agent, or build must render the honest state. A missing fact is a named gap — never 0, never implied success, never a silently omitted row. Per-record claims come from that record's own envelope, never from mutable current state (the temporal-drift class #1424 shipped and #1410 pinned). Streaming and persisted renderings must tell one story. Deterministic part of this rule: the surfaces below and their pinned honesty tests must keep existing; the conduct itself is held by review against docs/strategy/multi-agent-delivery-protocol.md §6 and proven by those tests in `npm run ci:fast`.
mustDo: Render an unknown value as a named gap ('not recorded', 'unavailable', and why), and pin that string in a test so it cannot decay into 0 or blank.
Read per-record claims (owner, agent, engine, model, permission posture, usage) from the record's own payload; live lookups are only valid for live state.
Keep the streaming row and the persisted row in parity, and extend the streaming-parity test when you touch either path.
mustNotDo: Do not coalesce an absent fact into 0, an empty string, or a dropped row.
Do not render a field no producer can populate — delete the claim instead (the #1426/#1430 structured-tools removal).
Do not describe a historical turn from current settings, current connection state, or Date.now().
explain.exampleGood: usage.totalTokens === undefined -> render 'tokens not recorded' and assert that copy in TurnProvenanceCard.test.tsx.
explain.exampleBad: {usage?.totalTokens ?? 0} tokens — a turn that never reported usage now claims it spent zero.

rules.message: Command-evidence routing matches an execution anchored to the leading command, and a partial-scope run never satisfies a full-scope claim.

explain.summary: Evidence services turn observed activity into claims, so a loose match manufactures proof. A claim pattern must anchor to the command actually executed at the head of the command line; a mention inside prose, an argument, or an echoed reminder must never route. A narrower run must not satisfy a wider claim — exclude it per pattern and let it fall through to the claim it does honestly support. A gate whose claim type no policy can produce is unreachable and must be diagnosed, not left silently waiting. Deterministic part of this rule: the routing policy, bridges, and their pinned tests must keep existing; `npm run ci:fast` runs those tests. PROMOTION TRIGGER (station#1480, replacing the original ~2026-08-15 date gate): this rule is assessed for `Require` when `docs/strategy/catches/catches.jsonl` records its first in-scope catch dated on or after 2026-08-01, the day the rule shipped — on evidence, never on a calendar date, because zero findings is absence of data and a second date would produce the same non-answer the first one did. In-scope classes under station#1480's mapping: `pipe-masked-exit`, `unexecuted-evidence`, `stale-evidence-as-fresh`. STATUS: the trigger has FIRED — `station-1555-tail-pipe-reported-a-commit-that-never-happened` (2026-08-03, `pipe-masked-exit`). The promotion itself is a separate human Protected Standards decision and is queued at station#1763; it is not taken here because it must repeat the artifact-tightening station#1480 required of `verification-conduct-sentinels-and-fault-injection` (promote only pins whose deletion would matter, and confirm the repo passes the tightened rule first). Disclosed dispute: `pipe-masked-exit` is also named verbatim by `verification-conduct-sentinels-and-fault-injection`'s own mustNotDo, so which rule owns that class is unsettled — a symptom of rules named for conduct that derive nothing (station#1762), not a reason to move the record.
mustDo: Anchor every command claim pattern to the start of the command line, and cover the near-miss (a mention, an argument, a quoted reminder) with a negative test.
Express scope narrowing as a per-pattern exclusion so an excluded command falls through to the lower claim it truthfully supports.
When a gate expects a claim type, prove some routable policy can produce it — surface an unreachable gate as a diagnostic instead of waiting forever.
mustNotDo: Do not route evidence from a command that was only read, printed, echoed, or planned.
Do not accept a focused or partial run as evidence for the repo's canonical lane (`npm run ci:fast`).
Do not widen a pattern, or relax a tool allowlist, to make a stuck gate advance.
explain.exampleGood: pattern: /^\s*npm\s+run\s+ci:fast\b/ with a test asserting `echo "run npm run ci:fast later"` does not route.
explain.exampleBad: pattern: /ci:fast/ — a comment about the lane becomes merge-readiness evidence.

rules.message: Joins, projections, and manifest reads resolve on an exact key or report unavailable naming every candidate — and they never write.

explain.summary: A projection is a claim about something else's state, so an ambiguous join resolved by 'newest wins' presents a coin flip as fact. Resolve on an exact key; when more than one candidate matches, report unavailable and name the candidates so a human can pick. A read path stays a read path: deriving, folding, and joining must not persist, backfill, or repair state, because an idempotent-looking write on a read still opens a lost-update window. And a capability is only claimable when a producer actually populates its field. Deterministic part of this rule: the join/fold modules and their pinned tests must keep existing; `npm run ci:fast` runs those tests. PROMOTION TRIGGER (station#1480, replacing the original ~2026-08-15 date gate): this rule is assessed for `Require` when `docs/strategy/catches/catches.jsonl` records its first in-scope catch dated on or after 2026-08-01, the day the rule shipped — on evidence, never on a calendar date, because zero findings is absence of data and a second date would produce the same non-answer the first one did. In-scope class under station#1480's mapping: `fail-open-validation`. STATUS: not fired — five records in the corpus, the most recent 2026-07-29, none since the rule shipped. When it fires, the promotion is still a human Protected Standards decision and must repeat the artifact tightening station#1480 required of `verification-conduct-sentinels-and-fault-injection`: promote only pins whose deletion would matter, and confirm the repo passes the tightened rule before arming it.
mustDo: Match join keys exactly, and return an explicit unavailable result listing every candidate when the match is ambiguous.
Keep fold, projection, and freshness functions pure — return the derived value and let a caller decide whether to persist it.
Record a disclosed gap in the module docstring when an upstream producer does not emit the field a claim would need (see flow-run-freshness.ts).
mustNotDo: Do not fuzzy-match, prefix-match, or pick the newest candidate to resolve ambiguity.
Do not write, backfill, or self-heal inside a read path, even when the write looks idempotent.
Do not derive a claim from a field no producer writes — report the gap instead.
explain.exampleGood: candidates.length === 1 ? candidates[0] : { status: 'unavailable', candidates: candidates.map((c) => c.id) }
explain.exampleBad: candidates.sort(byMtimeDesc)[0] — the newest match is presented as the answer, and the loser is never named.

rules.message: Verification evidence is captured in sentinel form, and a guard is only trusted once fault injection has proven it fails.

explain.summary: Wrapper exits, background-task notifications, and piped tails have all reported success for failed commands in this repo, so pass/fail must be captured by a sentinel the reporter reads back. A guard that has never been made to fail is unproven: commit the fix first (a restore silently wipes uncommitted work), inject at the guard the change claims to add, and restore byte-identically. An injection that is not caught is a stop signal, not a shrug — the two best finds of the codifying arc came from injections that failed to fail. Deterministic part of this rule, and the ONLY thing `Require` buys: deleting one of the five pinned artifacts below is a readiness FAIL (exit 1) instead of a warning. It does not make this rule detect the conduct it is named for — that is held by review against the protocol, and is tracked as a re-typing question on station#1762. The list was narrowed at promotion (station#1480) from seven entries to five: `scripts/` and `tests/` were dropped because `existsSync` on a directory is true while any file remains, so they could never fail; `scripts/run-verification.mjs`, `scripts/vitest-resource-manifest.mjs` and `tests/e2e-manifest.mjs` were dropped because each has many importers and the lane itself reds loudly the moment one goes missing; `docs/strategy/local-merge-readiness.md` was dropped because its retirement when provider-hosted CI returns is foreseeable and correct, and a rule that reds on a planned removal teaches bypass. The five kept entries are the ones a plausible future change could remove silently, in the same commit as whatever else references them.
mustDo: Capture pass/fail as `if <cmd>; then echo OK > x.exit; else echo FAILED > x.exit; fi` and report from the sentinel file.
Commit fixes before injecting a fault, restore with `git checkout -- <path>`, and prove byte-identity (`git diff` empty, or shasum against `git show HEAD:<path>`).
Treat an uncaught injection as a stop signal; report a deliberately uncaught one as a declared negative control.
mustNotDo: Do not use `cmd | tail -N`, a wrapper's exit, or a task notification as pass/fail evidence.
Do not `git stash` anywhere in this repo — the stash stack is shared by every worktree of this checkout.
Do not admit a check that can report green when its target is absent (conditional exits, `expect(true)`, silent optional locators).
explain.exampleGood: if npm run ci:fast; then echo OK > ci.exit; else echo FAILED > ci.exit; fi   # then read ci.exit
explain.exampleBad: npm run ci:fast | tail -5 — the tail's exit is what you read, so a red lane prints success.
